We set ourselves apart from other criminal defense law firms by providing passionate, courageous and innovative representation and full-service legal support with premium customer service.

In addition to results in criminal defense trials, we are widely-recognized experts in record clearing, Sex Offender Deregistration, judicial clemency, criminal appeals and other post-trial litigation.

Major Victories & Notoriety

We represent clients who face pending or threatened high-stakes litigation against the government. Our lawyers, Paul Saputo and Nicholas Toufexis, defend people against serious misdemeanor and felony charges in state and federal courts. The firm also handles a variety of civil matters related to criminal law, including record clearing and civil asset forfeiture. Learn more about our Notable Victories and Press Coverage

Client service is our priority, and we have been consistently awarded the AVVO Client’s Choice Award for excellent client service. We have stellar reviews >>

Our attorneys and staff are all dedicated criminal defense professionals. The firm is led by Paul Saputo, a highly accomplished, AV Rated “Preeminent” Texas criminal defense lawyer. Nicholas Toufexis is the firm’s Managing Partner, both representing clients inside and outside of the courtroom and managing the firm.

Mr. Saputo has represented people in many high-profile cases, including the Dallas Police Shooting case, where Mr. Saputo was able to garner his client’s release within hours, and the Twin Peaks Waco Biker case with all charges dismissed. In addition to leading Saputo Toufexis | Criminal Defense, he is a frequent contributor to various media outlets and is active within the bar association and politics. 

Because we are innovators in criminal law matters, many other criminal defense attorneys send us the difficult cases, and we are frequently hired by other attorneys to consult during trial, pretrial or post-trial litigation.

Learn more about our Notable Victories and Press Coverage

About Paul Saputo

We’re not just criminal defense lawyers, we are warriors fighting unjust and corrupt government prosecutions with a history of success and a reputation for tenacity, courage and legal ingenuity

Paul Saputo
Founding Partner

Awards & Recognition

Martindale-Hubbell awarded Paul Saputo a Martindale-Hubbell® Peer Review Rating™ of “AV” ”Preeminent” rating, which means that he was deemed to have very high professional ethics and preeminent legal ability. Only lawyers with the highest ethical standards and professional ability receive this Martindale-Hubbell Peer Review Rating.

Martindale-Hubbell awarded attorney Paul Saputo the “Client Champion” award. From Martindale:

Martindale-Hubbell’s new Client Champion awards recognize those attorneys who excel at service as affirmed by their clients. The awards, based on the quantity and quality of an attorney’s Martindale-Hubbell client reviews, demonstrate an ongoing commitment to delivering excellent client service.

Best Lawyers selected Mr. Saputo as a “Ones to Watch” in the White Collar Attorney practice area. Paul Saputo has also been named to the Texas Super Lawyers list. In addition, Paul Saputo has been selected in consecutive years to D Magazine’s Best Lawyers: Criminal Defense list and D Magazine’s Best Lawyers Under 40.

Paul Saputo has also achieved a perfect “10.0 – Top Attorney” rating on AVVO, multiple AVVO “Client’s Choice” awards and a “10.0” rating on Justia.

Since 2018, attorney Paul Saputo has also been awarded the “Best Business: Three Best Rated®” distinction. 

Background & Training

Mr. Saputo has practiced throughout Texas in more than fifty Texas state and federal courts. He has obtained hundreds of dismissals and acquittals for clients facing a wide array of serious charges. He has also developed groundbreaking innovations in defense strategies and tactics.

A member of the prestigious Texas Bar College, he continues to both train other lawyers in various continuing education seminars and attend many hours of continuous legal education on a yearly basis with some of the best lawyers, judges and law professors in the country. Mr. Saputo has delivered seminars on topics including “Legislative Updates,” “Advanced Record Clearing,” and other hot topics in criminal law. He is dedicated to defending people accused of crimes and courageously standing up to fight the government when lives and freedom are in jeopardy.

Mr. Saputo is a graduate of the elite Duke University School of Law, a nationally recognized top-ten law school in the United States. Before graduating law school, he worked for a Federal District Court Judge and wrote several appellate briefs for defendants in California challenging the medical marijuana laws of that state.

After law school, Mr. Saputo worked as an attorney at the internationally renowned law firm of Vinson & Elkins, LLP. While there Mr. Saputo helped represent some of the largest companies in the world and received high-level legal training. After leaving Vinson & Elkins, he worked for and with several of the leading criminal defense attorneys in the state of Texas before he founded the firm.

Now he brings his high-level legal training and experience to each one of his clients’ cases. And above all, his commitment to zealously representing his clients in court drives him to the great degree of success that he enjoys in the practice of criminal defense law.

Mr. Saputo is proud to represent some of the best clients in world. He is a deeply passionate attorney who believes that a fair trial is something that must be won through aggressive legal representation. While the process can be daunting, and in many ways unfair, he appreciates the opportunity to go to work for you and stand up for your rights – leveling the playing field and making sure that you are treated with the dignity and compassion that you deserve.

Memberships & Service

As an active member of many criminal defense organizations, Mr. Saputo maintains the highest level of professionalism, proficiency, knowledge and expertise in criminal law. He is a member of organizations including the Texas Bar Association, Texas Bar College, Dallas Criminal Defense Lawyers Association, Texas Criminal Defense Lawyers Association, the DUI Defense Lawyers Association, the Tarrant County Criminal Defense Lawyers Association and the Dallas Bar Association, among others.

Mr. Saputo currently is a past director and secretary of the Dallas Criminal Defense Lawyers Association.

We are active in many criminal defense and legal organizations, and we regularly contribute to the advancement of the criminal defense legal representation. Attorney Paul Saputo regularly presents continuing education seminars to other lawyers, judges and academics.

His “think outside the box” mentality has turned many negatives in cases into positives.

Mr. Toufexis is ready to go to work for you and ensure that your rights and freedoms are fully protected.
 
Mr. Toufexis is a member of the prestigious Texas Bar College, and he continues to better himself through numerous hours of continuous legal education, attending some of the most sought-after education from some of the best lawyers in Texas.

Hire the Firm

We know that when you need us, you are going through a traumatic experience, and we understand how important it is to you to have an attorney who will zealously represent you inside and outside of court. We understand that every aspect of your life may be in jeopardy, and we are here to help. When you become a client, you can leave your worry with us – we handle every aspect of your case. We strive to make sure you understand the entire process and all of the options that may be available to you.

Whether you have been arrested, charged or are under investigation, contact us immediately to protect your rights. The process is simple: book an appointment with us and tell us about your case in person or over the phone. If we agree to accept you as a client, we will quote you a fee and send you a contract to sign.

Please do not send the firm any confidential information about any matter until you receive a written or electronic notice from the firm advising you that the firm represents you (an “engagement letter”). When you receive an engagement letter from the firm, you will be the firm’s client, and we may exchange confidential information freely.

The firm accepts all forms of payment, including credit and debit cards, cash and checks.

Payment plans are welcome, and we also welcome active military and veterans with discounted rates.

When you hire Saputo Toufexis | Criminal Defense, our experienced criminal defense attorneys will review your case and analyze every detail to determine your best defense strategy. Whether we are representing you on a DWI charge, a possession of controlled substance case, a serious sex crime felony or in any other criminal prosecution, we conduct independent investigations, rigorously examine all the forensic evidence produced against you and advocate aggressively on your behalf.

Paul Saputo is the founding attorney of Saputo Toufexis, one of Dallas, Texas’s most respected criminal defense firms. Known for his relentless advocacy, innovative strategies, and unwavering commitment to protecting the rights of the accused, Paul has earned a reputation as a fearless trial lawyer and trusted advisor for clients facing the most serious criminal charges. His leadership has helped shape Saputo Toufexis into a powerhouse firm that consistently delivers results in high-stakes cases across Dallas and throughout Texas.

For Paul, criminal defense is more than a career; it is a mission. He has dedicated his professional life to standing against government overreach, protecting individual liberties, and ensuring that every client receives the strongest possible defense.

Professional Background

Paul Saputo’s path to becoming one of Dallas’s leading criminal defense attorneys began with a deep commitment to justice and a rigorous legal education. After earning his law degree, Paul quickly distinguished himself as a trial lawyer capable of handling complex and high-profile cases. His early career was marked by success in federal and state courts, where he developed a reputation for challenging the government at every turn.

Over the years, Paul has been recognized by peers, clients, and respected legal organizations alike. He has been named one of the Best Lawyers in Dallas by D Magazine and honored with the Silver Client Champion Award from Martindale-Hubbell, a recognition based on client reviews and satisfaction. These accolades reflect not only his legal skill but also his dedication to client service and ethical advocacy.

Legal Practice Areas

At Saputo Toufexis, Paul leads the firm’s criminal defense practice, overseeing a wide range of cases that demand precision, creativity, and courage. His practice areas include:

Criminal Defense: Representing clients in state and federal courts, Paul has defended individuals against charges ranging from misdemeanors to serious felonies. His ability to dismantle prosecution strategies has resulted in dismissals, acquittals, and reduced charges for countless clients.

Federal Crimes: Paul has extensive experience in federal court, where the stakes are often higher and the government’s resources more formidable. He has successfully defended clients accused of white-collar crimes, conspiracy, and other federal offenses.

DWI Defense: Recognizing the severe consequences of a DWI conviction, Paul has developed effective strategies to challenge evidence, question procedures, and protect clients’ driving privileges and reputations.

Drug Crimes: From possession to trafficking, Paul has defended clients against drug-related charges with a focus on constitutional protections, evidentiary challenges, and innovative defense strategies.

Through these practice areas, Paul has built a track record of success that speaks to his ability to handle even the most difficult cases.

Philosophy and Approach

Paul’s legal philosophy is rooted in the belief that every person deserves a defense that is as strong and determined as the government’s prosecution. He has never represented the government; his entire career has been devoted to defending people against it. This client-centered philosophy is at the heart of Saputo Toufexis’s mission.

Paul approaches each case with meticulous preparation, aggressive advocacy, and a willingness to challenge conventional thinking. He is known for filing innovative motions, developing creative trial strategies, and leveraging deep legal knowledge to protect his clients. His clients describe him as both compassionate and fearless. He is an attorney who listens, understands, and then fights tirelessly on their behalf.

Role in the Firm

As the founding attorney of Saputo Toufexis, Paul plays a central role in shaping the firm’s mission, strategy, and culture. He works closely with Nick Toufexis to ensure that every client benefits from the firm’s collective experience and resources. Under his leadership, the firm has grown into one of the most respected criminal defense practices in Dallas, handling some of the most complex and high-profile cases in Texas.

Paul’s responsibilities extend beyond trial work. He mentors younger attorneys, develops firm-wide defense strategies, and ensures that Saputo Toufexis remains at the cutting edge of criminal defense law. His vision has always been clear: to create a firm that stands as a shield against government power and a voice for those facing the weight of the criminal justice system.

Community Involvement

Beyond the courtroom, Paul is deeply committed to serving his community and advancing the cause of justice. He has contributed to legal education by sharing insights on criminal defense strategies, constitutional rights, and trial advocacy. His work has helped raise awareness about prosecutorial misconduct, government overreach, and the importance of protecting individual liberties.

Paul’s dedication to community service is reflected in his willingness to take on difficult cases that others might avoid. He believes that defending the accused is not just about winning cases. It is about upholding the principles of justice, fairness, and due process that form the foundation of our legal system.

Testimonials and Client Trust

The true measure of Paul’s impact can be found in the words of his clients. Posted on Mr. Saputo’s profile on Avvo.com, you will find quotes like:

“I was desperate. Paul called at 9pm. I wasn’t expecting an attorney to answer an online inquiry at that time. He guided us spot on.”

“I can’t thank him enough for everything he’s done, and if you need a true lawyer that will actually fight for you, don’t think twice before getting Paul Saputo, the best criminal defense lawyer out there!”

“We won our case and he did an excellent job in keeping my fiance informed throughout the process.”

These testimonials reflect the trust and confidence that clients place in Paul. For many, he is not just an attorney but a guide, an advocate, and a protector during one of the most difficult times in their lives.

Nicholas Toufexis is the Managing Partner of Saputo Toufexis | Criminal Defense PLLC, one of Texas’s premier criminal defense firms. With a reputation for sharp trial skills, meticulous preparation, and fierce client advocacy, Nick has established himself as a powerhouse in defending clients against high-stakes criminal charges in Dallas and throughout Texas. Alongside founding partner Paul Saputo, he leads a dedicated team focused on protecting the rights of the accused in state and federal courts.

Background and Education

Nick’s path to criminal defense is rooted in a decade of service in the United States Navy, where he served as a Corpsman, honing a tenacious fighting spirit that he now brings to the courtroom. After his military career, he pursued his legal education at SMU Dedman School of Law at Southern Methodist University. During law school, Nick interned under Paul Saputo, gaining invaluable hands-on experience in trial advocacy and challenging prosecutorial strategies. Upon graduation and licensure, he joined the firm as an associate, quickly rising to partner and eventually Managing Partner due to his exceptional talent, dedication, and results-driven approach.

His military background and legal training have instilled in him the values of preparation, creativity, and boldness, emphasizing that effective defense requires intelligent, courageous action when clients’ freedoms are on the line.

Career Milestones and Achievements

As Managing Partner, Nick has led the firm in handling complex cases ranging from misdemeanors to serious felonies and federal offenses, securing dismissals, acquittals, and favorable negotiations that preserve clients’ livelihoods, families, and reputations. His recognitions as a Super Lawyers Rising Star and Best Lawyers Ones to Watch underscore his excellence and growing prominence in the field. Nick has never represented the government; his entire career is devoted to safeguarding individuals from its overreach.

Key Practice Areas

Nick specializes in a broad spectrum of criminal defense matters, including:

  • General Criminal Defense: Misdemeanor and felony cases, with a track record of dismissals and acquittals.
  • DWI/DUI Defense: Aggressive challenges to evidence, protecting driving privileges and minimizing long-term consequences.
  • Drug Crimes: Defending against possession, trafficking, and related charges by scrutinizing searches, seizures, and constitutional violations.
  • Federal Crimes: Advanced strategies for federal offenses requiring deep legal expertise.
  • Military Law: Leveraging his Navy veteran experience to handle military-related legal issues.
  • Appeals and Post-Trial Litigation: Criminal appeals, record clearing, sex offender deregistration, and judicial clemency.
  • Other Related Matters: Civil asset forfeiture and matters intersecting criminal law.

Philosophy and Approach

Nick’s defense philosophy centers on tailored strategies, relentless preparation, and innovative thinking to turn case weaknesses into strengths. He views every client as deserving of a champion who will fight intelligently and compassionately against government power. From investigation to trial, Nick prepares as if every case will go to court, maximizing opportunities for the best outcomes while safeguarding constitutional rights and civil liberties.

Client Communication and Transparency

Clients value Nick’s clear communication, accessibility, and honesty during what is often the most stressful time in their lives. He prioritizes explaining the legal process, providing prompt updates, and building trust to empower clients throughout their cases. Testimonials reflect his impact:

“Nick did a great job! Was always available and very professional! I would recommend him and this law firm to any and everybody! If you find yourself in a bad situation and don’t think you have a way out! Hit Saputo Toufexis Law Firm and they will go to war for you! Thanks Nick I truly appreciate you and my family thank you!” – Deandre B.

“From start to finish, Nicholas Toufexis was very personable, educated, and hard working throughout my case. I believe he got me the best I could’ve gotten regarding my legal situation.” – Zach G.

“Nick Toufexis is an outstanding and confident attorney. Throughout the process he kept me informed and prepared me for the best possible outcome.” – Duron M.

Professional Involvement and Community Initiatives

Nick is actively engaged in the legal community, serving as co-chair of the Solo and Small Firms Committee for the Dallas Association of Young Lawyers. He is a member of the Texas Criminal Defense Lawyers Association, Dallas Criminal Defense Lawyers Association, and Texas Bar Association. His contributions extend to publications in legal journals like Headnotes, and he is committed to broader efforts in protecting the justice system’s integrity and advocating for fairness.

Nicholas Toufexis is more than an attorney—he is a dedicated advocate, strategic leader, and protector of justice. For those facing criminal charges in Dallas or across Texas, Nick and Saputo Toufexis stand ready to defend your rights with unmatched determination.

2024 “Terry Stop” Motion to Suppress GRANTED in Dallas DWI 2nd

In a significant victory for the legal team at Saputo Toufexis | Criminal Defense, a recent case involving a DWI 2nd has set a remarkable precedent in the interpretation and application of lawful detainment procedures. The client, who was immediately pulled out of her vehicle by law enforcement due to the visible presence of a Crown Royal bottle on the passenger side, faced a premature detention based on questionable grounds. During the cross-examination, it came to light that the officer’s decision to detain the client for a DWI investigation stemmed solely from the presence of the alcohol bottle, the client’s failure to lower the car radio volume, the way she had stored a weapon in the vehicle. A second officer corroborated this reasoning, adding that the client’s allegedly erratic behavior alongside the Crown Royal bottle prompted the immediate detention for DWI investigation.

The prosecution’s argument hinged on the “totality of the circumstances,” suggesting that the collective observations by the officers justified the suspicion of intoxication. However, when pressed during cross-examination, the officers were unable to provide concrete, articulable facts to support their belief that the client was under the influence. This gap in the prosecution’s case highlighted a crucial issue in law enforcement practices, where subjective interpretation can lead to unwarranted detainment.

The defense, led by the astute lawyers at Saputo Toufexis, skillfully argued that this scenario was a prime example of the concerns addressed in the landmark Terry v. Ohio case. The argument underscored the importance of officers having a clear, articulable basis for believing that someone is involved in criminal activity before detaining them. The judge, aligning with this perspective, granted the motion to suppress, affirming the importance of adhering to constitutional protections against unreasonable searches and seizures. This triumph not only marks a pivotal success for Saputo Toufexis | Criminal Defense but also reinforces the firm’s commitment to upholding justice and the fundamental rights of individuals.

2021 Not Guilty in Collin County

In one of the first trials since courts reopened after the Covid-19 pandemic, Paul Saputo tried his client’s case with Nick Toufexis against two of Collin County’s best misdemeanor prosecutors. The jury returned a Not Guilty verdict in less than 5 minutes.

2019 Not Guilty in Collin County DWI >0.15

Paul Saputo tried his client’s case alone against two formidable prosecutors in Collin County in late 2019. Facing a particularly high blood score, his client put his liberty on the line and went to the jury. We fought hard against stiff opposition from the state. Few of the judge’s rulings came back on our side, but we were nonetheless able to prevail. The jury returned a NOT GUILTY verdict after 2 days of deliberation.

2019 Not Guilty in Dallas County Indecency with a Child

Paul Saputo and Rob Keating tried an Indecency with a Child case to a jury in May 2019 in Dallas County. The jury returned a Not Guilty verdict on the indicted offense of Indecency with a Child. Unfortunately, the jury returned a Guilty verdict on a lesser included offense of Attempted Indecency, which the state asked for mid-trial. The case is currently on appeal.

Oral Argument at the United States Federal 5th Circuit Court of Appeals on Prosecutorial Misconduct Claim arising out of Northern District of Texas

The Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals granted oral argument on a case that Paul Saputo tried in 2016 in the Northern District of Texas. We appealed the verdict, arguing that the significant prosecutorial misconduct should have required the federal district court judge to dismiss the case.

We were able to show that the FBI’s digital forensic expert had allowed multiple gigabytes of data to overwrite critical data on our client’s hard drive, and the only place where we could look for clues (the master file table) had also been corrupted while in FBI custody because the forensic analyst had allowed a defrag process to execute.

None of this was initially disclosed to the defense, although it was eventually admitted at trial on cross-examination by Mr. Paul Saputo.

2018 Not Guilty in Martin County Aggravated Assault with a Deadly Weapon on a Peace Officer

Paul Saputo and Rob Keating traveled to Martin County in 2018 to try an Aggravated Assault with a Deadly Weapon case. Our client had already plead guilty, under the advice of his old attorney, without the benefit of any plea bargain offer. He was facing life in prison. As soon as we took over the case, we filed a motion for to change his plea to Nor Guilty, and we set the case for trial.

Our client had engaged in a standoff with police in Stanton, Texas. Ultimately Midland S.W.A.T. was engaged, along with an armored vehicle, to end the standoff. Our client was accused of shooting at a police officer.

We were able to hire and expert to evaluate the alleged “bullet holes.” Our expert was able to reproduce the material into which the bullets were allegedly shot, and conclude, after an independent experiment, that the holes were likely not caused by bullets

At trial, the state’s case fell apart as we were able to cast doubt on each of the witnesses’ testimony. In the middle of trial, the state offered a fantastic plea bargain, five years deferred adjudication probation. We turned it down and went to the jury.

The jury returned a quick NOT GUILTY verdict, and our client walked free.

Not Guilty in 2018 Dallas County DWI Trial

In Dallas County Criminal Court 9, a jury returned a Not Guilty verdict in a DWI case that we had worked on for three years. It was a hard-fought case involving a major accident.

Client cleared in Dallas Police Shooting wrongful accusation

Our client was wrongfully accused by the Dallas Police Department of shooting several police officers during a peaceful protest in downtown Dallas in 2016. For a time he was among the most wanted men in the United States. We were retained late in the evening after he turned himself into authorities, and we were able to quickly find evidence and secure his release.

Federal sentencing results in 10 Year Downward Deviation from Sentencing Guidelines in 2018

Judge Lynn granted our client a 10-year downward deviation from the federal sentencing guidelines. Such deviations are very rare in a federal sentencing case. Deviations are different from departures. A guideline departure is a considered within the framework of the guidelines, while a deviation has no basis in the guidelines. A deviation is rarer than a departure.

Not Guilty Jury Verdict for client originally accused of Intoxication Manslaughter

Our client in this case was originally charged with Intoxication Manslaughter. After quick action by our legal and investigative team, we were able to find evidence that our client was not the driver of the vehicle. The Dallas District Attorney’s Office refused to drop the charges, and so we went to trial. After a highly-contested trial, the jury returned a Not Guilty verdict.

The state then proceeded to seek a conviction for misdemeanor DWI. We filed a motion to dismiss pursuant to the Double Jeopardy clause, arguing that a jury had already returned a verdict indicating that our client was not the driver of the vehicle. The judge agreed and ultimately dismissed the case. To date, the real driver of the vehicle has not faced prosecution.

Case Dismissed after picking jury in Aggravated Sexual Assault of Child case in 2017

The day after jury selection in a Dallas prosecution for Aggravated Sexual Assault of a Child, our client was offered a misdemeanor assault reduction. We turned it down and demanded a trial. The district attorney then immediately dismissed the case. More than two years of litigation resulted in long-overdue justice for our client. Tough case, meet tough defense attorney.

United States Attorney dismisses case against client charged in El Paso Federal Court with Possession of Child Pornography

Our client was charged in an El Paso federal court with Receipt and Distribution of Material Involving the Sexual Exploitation of Children and Possession of Material Involving the Sexual Exploitation of Children in Cause No. EP-16-CR0860. After we discovered discrepancies between what the FBI and DHS asked a judge to search and what they actually searched, we filed a Motion to Suppress Evidence based on a violation of our client’s Constitutional rights. Instead of having a hearing on the issue, the United States Attorney’s Office decided to dismiss the case, allowing federal authorities to save face.

ALL CHARGES DISMISSED against our client in the Twin Peaks Waco Biker case

In 2015, nine people were killed in a shootout at a Twin Peaks in Waco, Texas. There has been extensive press coverage related to this case.

On April 4, 2019, all charges against our client were dismissed!

Client “No-billed” by grand jury investigating shooting death case

Our client used deadly force during the course of his duty. We represented the client before and during a grand jury investigation. After almost a year, the Dallas County grand jury refused to return an indictment. Instead, our client was “no-billed” and cleared of all charges.

Judge returns a Directed Verdict of Acquittal in case involving trainer of professional athletes

Our client was an athletic trainer who had worked with numerous professional athletes. He was charged with assaulting a public servant and several other related charges. During a jury trial in Dallas County, attorney Paul Saputo requested that the court return a directed verdict of Not Guilty. After heated argument between defense counsel and the state prosecuting attorney, the judge agreed with defense counsel and granted a directed verdict of acquittal. Soon after, the Dallas District Attorney’s Office chose to drop all remaining charges.

Rare Not Guilty verdict in Rockwall County DWI

Our client was charged with Driving While Intoxicated in Rockwall County, a county with a notably high DWI conviction rate. Our client decided to try the case, and we were able to obtain a Not Guilty verdict. The state had blood evidence indicating a high blood alcohol concentration level, but the state’s lab procedures in the cases were called into question. The jury returned its verdict after approximately two hours of deliberation.

2016 Dismissal of Fort Worth Federal Possession of Obscene Visual Representation of the Sexual Abuse of Children

Our client was facing prosecution in the Fort Worth Division of the United States District Court for the Northern District of Texas for Possession of Obscene Visual Representation of the Sexual Abuse of Children in 2016. After hours of argument in federal court, we were able to secure the pretrial release of our client. We attacked the accusation on several grounds, including the jurisdiction of the charge. The United States Attorney’s Office subsequently filed a motion to dismiss the charge.

Hill County Money Laundering case Dismissed and civil asset forfeiture assets returned

Our client was charged with Money Laundering, DWI and Possession of Controlled Substance in Hill County after a traffic stop turned into a major arrest. The state also attempted to seize several thousands dollars of our client’s money through a civil asset forfeiture action. The case was set for trial. Prior to trial, we were able to convince the District Attorney’s Office to drop all felony charges and return most of our client’s money. In the end, our client accepted a plea bargain deal on the DWI case alone that required him to be on probation and pay a fine. All felony charges were dismissed.

Faced with two charges of child molestation in Montague County, our client was facing the serious possibility of dying in prison. We vigorously fought the charges, with our client asserting his absolute innocence. On the eve of trial, we were able to convince the Montague County District Attorney to drop the charges. Our client ended up instead pleading guilty to two misdemeanor simple assault charges.

Si buscas al mejor

Abogado de Defensa Criminal en Dallas

en el área de Dallas o en cualquier otro lugar de Texas, los abogados Paul Saputo y Nick Toufexis quieren conocerte.

Con más de una década de experiencia en defensa criminal, nuestro equipo ha defendido exitosamente a clientes en algunos de los casos más desafiantes en Dallas y en todo Texas. Desde juicios de alto riesgo por agresión sexual hasta cargos federales graves, hemos asegurado desestimaciones, absoluciones y sentencias reducidas que han permitido a nuestros clientes seguir adelante con sus vidas.

Nuestra reputación está respaldada por el reconocimiento de las principales autoridades legales. Paul Saputo ha sido nombrado como uno de los Mejores Abogados en Dallas por D Magazine y honrado con el Premio Silver Client Champion de Martindale-Hubbell por su servicio excepcional a los clientes. Paul Saputo también ha logrado una calificación perfecta de “10.0 – Abogado Top” en AVVO, múltiples premios “Client’s Choice” de AVVO y una calificación de “10.0” en Justia. Best Lawyers seleccionó a Nicholas Toufexis como uno de los “Ones to Watch” en el área de práctica de Abogados de DWI/DUI en 2025. El Sr. Toufexis también recibió el premio Texas Super Lawyers Rising Stars el mismo año. Estos reconocimientos reflejan lo que nuestros clientes ya saben: luchamos incansablemente, pensamos estratégicamente y nunca nos echamos para atrás ante un desafío.

¿Enfrentando Cargos Criminales en Dallas? Por Qué Elegir al Abogado de Defensa Criminal Adecuado en Dallas Importa

Si enfrentas cargos criminales en Dallas, contratar al abogado de defensa criminal adecuado en Dallas puede ser la decisión más importante que tomes en tu vida. Ya sea que estés bajo investigación o enfrentando un proceso en curso, necesitas un abogado capacitado en quien puedas confiar.

Aunque todos tienen derecho a un abogado designado por el tribunal después de ser arrestados, el estándar para los abogados designados por el tribunal es una representación mínima “constitucionalmente efectiva”.

Este estándar también podría considerarse prácticamente inútil. Los mejores abogados criminales hacen más que solo entender la ley y los procedimientos judiciales para “guiarte” a través del proceso…

…los mejores abogados de defensa criminal en Dallas contraatacan.

El sistema de justicia criminal en Texas puede ser más que solo “complejo” y “difícil de navegar”. El sistema puede ser injusto, corrupto, fraudulento, opaco, engañoso y destructivo. Desde el momento en que estás siendo interrogado o puesto bajo arresto, tus derechos y tu libertad están en riesgo.

Las consecuencias de una acusación criminal pueden ser rápidas y transformadoras —amenazando tu trabajo, familia, libertad, tu futuro y, a veces, tu vida. Mereces un abogado veterano que luche incansablemente por tus mejores intereses.

Cómo encontrar a los mejores abogados de defensa criminal en Dallas, Texas

En Saputo Toufexis, buscamos clientes que quieran contratar a los mejores abogados de defensa criminal en Texas. Sigue leyendo para saber por qué esos clientes nos han contratado y por qué tú también deberías hacerlo.

Algunos abogados han trabajado para meter a la gente en la cárcel. Nosotros hemos dedicado toda nuestra carrera a mantener a la gente fuera.

Nuestros clientes no quieren contratar a un exfiscal. Quieren contratar a alguien que siempre haya luchado por proteger los derechos de los acusados.

No quieres estar dudando de qué lado está realmente tu abogado. Sabemos cómo piensan los fiscales porque los enfrentamos todos los días. Sabemos qué pasa detrás de puertas cerradas y cómo operan.

Nuestro objetivo es ser los mejores y más agresivos abogados defensores penales de Texas. Nunca nos hemos alineado con el gobierno. Estamos de su lado y solo del suyo.

Nuestro enfoque en la representación legal solo es igualado por nuestro compromiso con el servicio al cliente. No solo te preparamos para tus fechas en la corte —nos preparamos para ganar.

La misión de nuestra oficina legal es proporcionar una representación poderosa y basada en principios a clientes que enfrentan cargos criminales en el condado de Dallas y en todo el estado de Texas.

Defensa pura. Sin historial de fiscalía. Solo una defensa incansable por tu libertad.

Los abogados de defensa criminal en Dallas Paul Saputo y Nick Toufexis han dedicado toda su carrera legal a defender a las personas de los procesamientos gubernamentales. 

Más de una década de lucha – y mucho más por delante

Con más de una década de experiencia proporcionando asesoramiento legal personalizado y defendiendo a clientes frente al sistema legal, somos conocidos por obtener resultados. Hemos ganado una reputación por nuestra tenacidad, desafiando las acusaciones gubernamentales de frente.

Así es como nuestra firma de abogados ha establecido un historial probado de éxito en los tribunales de Texas. Como asesores legales experimentados, nuestros principales abogados de defensa criminal en Dallas aplican tácticas legales de vanguardia, extraídas de años de experiencia real en juicios.

Nuestra reputación habla por sí sola

No tomes nuestra palabra. Explora nuestras reseñas. Mira los premios que hemos ganado. Examina nuestros resultados y nuestro historial de éxito.

Nuestra historia destacada incluye la representación de numerosos clientes de alto perfil y victorias notables de alto perfil. Pero también hemos resuelto muchos otros casos de manera silenciosa y fuera de la vista del público. No importa el caso o el cliente, luchamos para mantener a nuestros clientes fuera de la custodia gubernamental.

Capacitamos a otros abogados.

Publicamos el análisis líder en la industria del código penal, actualizado cada sesión legislativa. ¡Los abogados leen lo que escribimos, los jueces también. Incluso los fiscales leen nuestras publicaciones!

Revisa nuestro análisis completo del código penal – escrito y actualizado a mano cada año desde 2015. También hemos publicado extensamente sobre temas que incluyen las directrices de sentencia federal, extradición y derecho constitucional.

Practicamos en todo el estado – no solo en Dallas, TX

Hemos representado a clientes en asuntos de juicio en más de 50 condados en Texas. Esta experiencia nos brinda más experiencia en la sala de audiencias, más tiempo en juicios y una comprensión más profunda de cómo ganar en una amplia gama de casos. No importa dónde estén tus cargos, mereces un abogado probado en todo el estado.

Practicamos regularmente en tribunales federales y estatales – y no solo en Texas – ¡hemos sido admitidos en tribunales federales en Luisiana, Oklahoma, Utah e incluso Wyoming!

¿Qué Tipos de Casos Criminales Manejamos en Nuestra Firma de Abogados?

Representamos a clientes en Dallas, TX, en una amplia gama de delitos criminales y otros asuntos relacionados:

⸻

Cargos por DWI/DUI

Nuestro profundo conocimiento de los métodos de pruebas de sobriedad en el campo, la ciencia de pruebas de aliento y sangre, y las protecciones constitucionales relacionadas con investigaciones de DWI nos ayuda a combatir casos de DWI para clientes. Esta experiencia es especialmente crítica porque los arrestos por DWI a menudo ocurren en carreteras principales como I-35E, I-635, U.S. 75 (Central Expressway) y el Dallas North Tollway, donde el Departamento de Policía de Dallas y el Departamento de Seguridad Pública de Texas frecuentemente realizan paradas de tráfico y patrullas de DWI.

Entendemos cómo las cortes del Condado de Dallas manejan las persecuciones por DWI, porque hemos pasado mucho tiempo en el Edificio de Cortes Frank Crowley luchando por nuestros clientes. Conocemos a los jueces locales, fiscales y procedimientos que pueden impactar significativamente un caso. La ley de Texas requiere que los conductores se sometan a pruebas químicas bajo el estatuto de consentimiento implícito del estado (Código de Transporte de Texas § 724.011), pero los conductores aún tienen derechos importantes respecto a pruebas de sobriedad en el campo, pruebas de aliento y extracciones de sangre.

Dado que los fiscales de Dallas dependen en gran medida de pruebas de sobriedad estandarizadas y evidencia química, escrutamos cada paso de la investigación en busca de violaciones constitucionales, procedimientos de prueba inadecuados o fallos en la forma en que se recolectó y presentó la evidencia. Esta visión local nos permite construir defensas sólidas para clientes que enfrentan cargos por DWI en Dallas.

⸻

Delitos de Drogas

Los cargos relacionados con drogas en Dallas pueden variar desde posesión hasta tráfico y manufactura. Construimos defensas agresivas para desafiar búsquedas ilegales y proteger tus derechos en las cortes del Condado de Dallas.

⸻

Casos de Asalto, Asalto Agravado y Violencia Doméstica

Los delitos de asalto incluyen infracciones menores como Asalto (por contacto o que resulte en lesiones corporales) y Asalto – Violencia Familiar (violencia doméstica), así como cargos por delitos graves como Asalto Agravado. Tanto el asalto agravado como el asalto simple pueden llevar a la encarcelación, órdenes de protección e incluso la deportación para no ciudadanos.

⸻

Robo Menor y Mayor

En Dallas, los cargos por robo bajo el Código Penal de Texas § 31.03 involucran “apropiarse ilegalmente” de propiedad con la intención de privar al dueño. ¿Cómo Puede Nuestra Oficina Legal Defenderte Contra Cargos Criminales en Texas?

El sistema legal no está diseñado para que las personas lo naveguen solas. Los fiscales buscan agresivamente condenas, y los plazos llegan rápido. Por eso, contar con una representación legal experimentada puede marcar toda la diferencia.

¿Qué Hace un Abogado de Defensa Criminal?

Un abogado de defensa criminal veterano proporciona estrategia legal, análisis de casos y defensa en la sala de audiencias. Desde el momento en que somos contratados, nuestro equipo evalúa toda la evidencia, investiga las afirmaciones de la fiscalía y diseña un plan de defensa a medida. También proporcionamos asesoramiento sobre los posibles resultados del juicio, rangos de sentencia y opciones de negociación de acuerdos, ayudando a nuestros clientes a tomar decisiones informadas en cada paso.

Realizamos investigaciones, presentamos mociones para suprimir evidencia inconstitucional, negociamos con fiscales y preparamos estrategias integrales para el juicio. Si ya has hablado con las fuerzas del orden sin un abogado presente, evaluamos cualquier declaración para determinar su admisibilidad y violaciones constitucionales.

Investigando y Construyendo la Defensa Temprano

Cuando se te acusa de un delito, las decisiones que tomas al principio del caso pueden moldear todo el resultado. Para los clientes que acuden a nosotros durante una investigación en curso, podemos intervenir para ayudar a evitar que se presenten cargos formales. 

Inmediatamente después del arresto, nuestros abogados comienzan a recopilar información. Esto incluye entrevistar a testigos, revisar imágenes de cámaras corporales y analizar informes policiales. Es esencial que la defensa comience temprano y no deje piedra sin mover. De hecho, muchos casos exitosos se ganan no en la corte, sino en las semanas previas —durante esta fase intensiva de investigación.

¿Cómo Desafiamos la Evidencia y Protegemos Tus Derechos?

En cada caso criminal, el gobierno tiene la carga de probar la culpabilidad más allá de una duda razonable —pero eso no significa que jueguen limpio. En Saputo Toufexis, una de nuestras estrategias más efectivas es desafiar la evidencia antes de que llegue a un jurado. Este tipo de trabajo de defensa proactivo puede llevar a que la evidencia sea descartada por completo, a que los casos sean desestimados o a que los cargos se reduzcan significativamente.

Hemos encontrado que los fiscales frecuentemente intentan admitir evidencia obtenida bajo circunstancias cuestionables, esperando que la defensa no contraataque.

Pero nuestros abogados de defensa criminal expertos contraatacan —y con fuerza.

Comenzamos cada caso analizando cómo las fuerzas del orden recolectaron y manejaron la evidencia. Examinamos si la policía tenía causa probable para buscar, si alguna orden judicial era válida y si los procedimientos se siguieron con precisión. Si los oficiales violaron tus derechos constitucionales —a través de búsquedas ilegales, confesiones coaccionadas o no leerte tus derechos Miranda— puedes tener derecho a presentar una moción para suprimir.

Nuestros abogados de defensa criminal experimentados también evalúan cómo la fiscalía planea interpretar la evidencia. Por ejemplo, las imágenes de cámaras corporales y las llamadas al 911 pueden ser distorsionadas o sacadas de contexto. Nuestra labor es replantear esa evidencia, exponer sus debilidades y asegurar que los jurados entiendan qué pasó realmente.

Usamos testigos expertos y técnicas de contrainterrogatorio para desentrañar circunstancias complejas y presentar una narrativa alternativa clara. A veces, la defensa más poderosa no es argumentar que el delito no ocurrió —es mostrar que el gobierno malinterpretó su propia evidencia.

¿Qué Deberías Esperar del Sistema de Justicia Criminal en Texas?

Cada caso criminal conlleva el riesgo de consecuencias severas —desde encarcelamiento y multas hasta el estigma de por vida de una condena. Ya sea que acabes de ser arrestado o ya tengas una audiencia en la corte acercándose, la complejidad del proceso legal puede volverse abrumadora rápidamente.

Navegar por el sistema de justicia en Texas puede ser una de las experiencias más intimidantes y confusas de la vida de una persona. Afortunadamente, nuestros abogados de defensa criminal experimentados están aquí para ayudarte a darle sentido —y tomar el control de tu caso.

Tu equipo en Saputo Toufexis proporciona una representación integral en cada etapa de un caso. Cuando contratas nuestra oficina legal, no solo obtienes un abogado de defensa criminal en Dallas – obtienes nuestro personal experimentado, investigadores y una amplia red legal.

Creemos en desafiar cada suposición —recuerda, eres inocente a menos que se pruebe tu culpabilidad más allá de una duda razonable.

Negociación Estratégica y Preparación para el Juicio

Una vez que hemos construido una ventaja a través de una estrategia de defensa sólida, entablamos negociaciones con la fiscalía. No solo aparecemos —nuestros abogados de defensa criminal en Dallas construyen narrativas de juicio alrededor de desafíos legales, problemas de credibilidad y violaciones constitucionales.

¿Cómo Funciona el Proceso Legal Después de Ser Arrestado?

Después de un arresto en Texas, el proceso legal comienza rápidamente —y tu defensa también debería hacerlo.

Presentación de Casos y Acusación del Gran Jurado

En algunos casos, hemos ayudado a clientes a evitar cargos por completo interviniendo antes de que comience el proceso del gran jurado. Si alguna vez eres contactado por las fuerzas del orden, siempre ten un abogado presente —incluso si eres inocente.

Desde la Primera Audiencia hasta la Disposición Final

La primera audiencia en los casos criminales del condado de Dallas suele ser una comparecencia, donde un magistrado establece una fianza. Un abogado de defensa criminal en Dallas puede ofrecer representación legal de inmediato para abogar por una fianza reducida o incluso una liberación por reconocimiento personal.

Una vez que estés en libertad bajo fianza, se te darán una serie de fechas en la corte. Estas pueden incluir conferencias previas al juicio, audiencias de evidencia, negociaciones de acuerdos y, finalmente, el juicio.

El gobierno puede comenzar a ofrecer acuerdos de culpabilidad, presentar mociones y, sin un abogado de defensa experimentado a tu lado, es fácil cometer un error.

Por Qué la Fase Previa al Juicio es Tan Crítica en el Derecho Penal

Muchos clientes piensan que su día en la corte es cuando comienza el juicio con jurado. En verdad, las batallas más decisivas a menudo ocurren semanas o meses antes del juicio —en audiencias de mociones, procedimientos de supresión o desafíos de evidencia. What are the laws in Texas for Aggravated Sexual Assault?

  • The laws in Texas for Aggravated Sexual Assault are Texas Penal Code §22.021[1]. These laws prohibit violent sexual assault and sexual assault that uses the the threat of violence as well as sexual assault committed through means of using a substance to alter the victim’s mental state. These laws also prohibit any sexual contact with persons under the age of 14 year old, the elderly and the disabled. In addition, the Texas Aggravated Sexual Assault laws provide a defense to prosecution that the sexual contact was performed for medical care. The laws in Texas for Aggravated Sexual Assault provide that the offense is a first degree felony and provide for enhanced penalties in some situations.

What is a Class C Assault in Texas?

  • A Class C Assault in Texas is a type of assault that is punishable under the criminal code only as a low-level misdemeanor. It is important to remember that just because it is punishable only as a low-level misdemeanor does not mean that it cannot be devastating for someone’s life. It can cause an employer to fire you, career loss, serious immigration consequences like deportation, denial of firearm rights, loss of visitation rights, among many other serious consequences.
  • Class C Assault in Texas comprises two types of assault. The first is Assault by Threat (Penal Code §22.01(a)(2)[2]), wherein the state would accuse you of threatening imminent bodily injury. The second is Assault by Offensive Contact (Penal Code §22.01(a)(3)[3]). This type of Class C assault occurs when someone contacts another person, causes the other person to feel “offended,” but without causing any further bodily injury.

What are the theft laws in Texas?

  • The theft laws in Texas are primarily Texas Penal Code §31.03. These laws don’t just prohibit “stealing,” they are much more expansive. They prohibit you from the unlawful appropriation of someone else’s property if you intend to deprive them of that property. The elements of the offense require that the state to prove that someone else actually owned some property, that you “appropriated” the property, that the appropriation was “unlawful” and that you had the state of mind to do that act intentionally (as opposed to mistakenly, for instance).[4]
  • The theft laws in Texas go into detail about what “unlawful appropriation” means. There are three different ways in which appropriation (which essentially means taking control over something) is unlawful: “(1) it is without the owner’s effective consent; (2) the property is stolen and the actor appropriates the property knowing it was stolen by another; or (3) property in the custody of any law enforcement agency was explicitly represented by any law enforcement agent to the actor as being stolen and the actor appropriates the property believing it was stolen by another.”[5]

What are the penalties for engaging in organized criminal activity in Texas?

  • The exact penalties for engaging in organized criminal activity in Texas vary depending on the nature of what kind of “criminal activity” the offender organized. In general, the penalty is one category higher than the most serious offense that was organized. So for instance, if the organized criminal activity was Class B theft, then the penalty for engaging in organized Class B theft would be the penalty range for Class A misdemeanors (up to one year in jail and up to a $4,000 fine).[6]
  • However, there are exceptions to this general rule regarding penalties for engaging in organized criminal activity. The penalty jumps up to a first degree felony and punishable by life without parole, for certain organized aggravated sexual assault charges.[7] The penalty jumps up to a first degree felony and punishable by a minimum of 30 years in prison if the organized activity was continuous smuggling of persons and someone who was smuggled died, was seriously injured or sexually assaulted.[8] If the underlying criminal activity was any other first degree felony, the penalty jumps up to a minimum fifteen years in prison.[9]
  • Another exception to this general rule regarding penalties for engaging in organized criminal activity concerns conspiracies. While conspiracies are usually punished lower than the underlying offense that was conspired, if the conspiracy was the basis of the engaging in organized criminal activity charge, the conspiracy is punished as if what was conspired had actually been achieved.[10]

What are the penalties in Texas for being charged with indecency with a child?

  • The penalties in Texas for Indecency with a Child vary depending on the subsection of the statute on which your conviction was based, and the prison time can be up to either ten or twenty years (with a minimum of two years regardless of which section applies). In addition, the penalties include mandatory registration on the sex offender list, even if you are not convicted and instead take deferred adjudication.
  • Indecency with a Child is punished as a second degree felony if the conviction is based on subsection (a)(1) (Sexual Contact), carrying a prison range between two and twenty years. Indecency with a Child is punished as a third degree felony if it is charged under subsection (a)(2) (Exposure), carrying a prison range between two and ten years.
  • However, the prison sentence may also be probated, in which case you would serve “community supervision” subject to restrictions placed on you as a condition of probation.

Have you or a loved-one been recently arrested? Here is what you need to know.

What to do if you’re Arrested in Texas

If you have been arrested, the first thing you will want to do is to post bond and get out of jail. If you can’t make bail in texas, you will likely be stuck in jail for some time.

EVERYTHING YOU NEED TO KNOW AFTER YOU’VE BEEN ARRESTED

  • How long do you stay in jail if you can’t make bail in texas?
  • How do you get someone out of jail?
  • What are the different kinds of bonds?
  • What is a PR Bond?
  • What is a Surety Bond?
  • What is a Cash Bond?
  • Can I get a bond amount reduced?
  • What can I do while out on bail?
  • Can I travel while out on bail?
  • When do you need to hire a criminal defense lawyer?
  • When do I have to go to court?
  • Is my driver’s license suspended?

It is critically important that you retain a criminal lawyer as soon as possible. You should call us before you talk to the police and before you have been formally booked in to jail. If you or your loved-one has been arrested and is already been booked into jail, you can retain us to help navigate the bail process, fight to get bail reduced and assist with a variety of other concerns you may have.

The first question most people have after an arrest is how to get out of jail. This is done through having a bond set and posting the bond in order to get out on bail. Bail is the mechanism by which a criminal court “restrains your liberty” to make sure you go to court when you are supposed to go to court. Everyone who is arrested is entitled to consideration for bail. An independent judge is supposed to set a bond in a “reasonable” amount to guarantee that you will go to court as required. Bond is set at an amount of money, and it may be either a cash bond, a surety bond or a PR bond. The court may also impose other restrictions such as electronic monitoring, an ignition interlock device for your car (or another kind of alcohol-monitoring device) if you are on bail for DWI, travel restrictions, restrictions on who you may interact with or any number of other options.

If the police want to interrogate you, you will be faced with the choice about whether or not to cooperate. That first choice has many severe implications, no matter what you choose or what you end up saying–it is always complicated and can have many long-term effects on your case and on your reputation and future. This is only the first choice that you will face. If you choose to cooperate with a police interrogation, you will need to be able to understand what questions are legitimate and which are crossing a line. If you choose to ignore the police, you risk losing an opportunity to make the case go away before arrest. This is always a decision you should make with the assistance of a lawyer, even if you are innocent.

If your loved-one has been arrested, you will need to post a bond to get him or her out of jail unless a judge grants a PR bond. Typically you will have to hire a criminal defense attorney to get a PR bond granted. If bail is not posted and the district attorney pursues charges, he or she will remain in jail until the case is finally resolved. You do not need a criminal attorney to post bond, but an attorney can help reduce the amount of bond and help you navigate the bail system.

Bail works very differently in the state court system than it does in the federal court system. In the federal court system, there is typically no money bail, and the decision about whether to release you pending trial is done in a detention hearing.

In addition to bail issues, there are numerous other decisions to make if you have been recently arrested. We will need to decide whether you are going to cooperate with the police investigation, whether you are going to conduct a parallel investigation alongside the police, whether you are going to give information to the district attorney’s office in an attempt to get the charges dismissed, whether you want an examining trial, whether you want to request an ALR hearing (for DWI charges) and many other considerations. These decisions will be crucial as the case progresses. A criminal defense attorney will provide you with advice and assistance in making these decisions.

Need help with a recent arrest? Contact us today to discuss legal representation.

or Text or Call (888) 239-9305

How long do you stay in jail if you can’t make bail in texas?

If you can’t make bail in Texas, you will stay in jail until you have served your sentence in full, have completely beaten your case through a not guilty verdict or dismissal, or until you are released on probation.

To finally resolve a case, it can take anywhere from a few months to a few years. Criminal cases usually go much better for defendants when the defendants are not being held in jail. If there is any way you can reduce your bond to get out of jail, that should be your first priority.

When people ask us, “What do i do if I’m arrested in Texas?” we usually interpret this to mean how to make bail. But there are many other considerations as well.

How do you get someone out of jail?

In general, you have to post a bond to get someone out of jail. We may be able to help you by getting a bond amount reduced or by obtaining a PR bond so that no money has to be paid to the court at all. You can post bond yourself or you can hire a bail bonds company. A criminal defense attorney can post a bond for you as well. The decision about which bail bond company you choose will be important as well. A bad bail bond company can make your life miserable.

What are the different kinds of bonds?

Texas law describes several different kinds of bonds, but the most popular types of bonds are surety bonds, cash bonds and PR bonds. The best kind of bond is a PR bond. Cash bonds are the hardest to post because you have to present cash to the court. Surety bonds are posted by bail bonds companies, and they only charge you a fraction of the amount of the bond. But this is a fee that you will not get back after the case is over.

What is a PR Bond?

A PR bond is a type of bail bond that does not require you to post any money up front or to hire a surety bail bond company. Essentially it is just a written promise that you will show up to court, and the contract specifies that you will owe the court a certain amount of money if you do not go to court as required.

What is a Surety Bond?

A surety bond is a type of bond that does not require an up-front payment to the court, but only licensed sureties may post this type bond. So you will have to hire a bail bond company to post this kind of bond, and they will charge you a fee for this. However, we can sometimes get these types of bonds converted to a much less expensive cash bond. If we get it converted, then you will get the cash back after the case is finally over.

Bail bond companies also usually require their own conditions, and if you break your contract with them, they may attempt to “off-bond” with you and if the court grants their request, your bond will be revoked and a warrant will be issued for your arrest.

What is a Cash Bond?

A cash bond is a type of bond that requires payment of the entire bond amount up front to the court and in cash. However, at the end of the case you will get your money back. In Dallas county, the person who posted the bond will receive the bond back in the form of a check sent via mail to the address that the person gave when posting bail in the first place. You will need to get an affidavit signed to have the bond sent elsewhere.

Can I get a bond amount reduced?

A criminal defense attorney can help you get your bond amount reduced by petitioning the judge and holding a hearing. Our criminal lawyer has had success getting bonds lowered and getting bonds reinstated after they have been revoked. In a recent case we were able to get reversed a denial of bail in federal court and obtained a property bond. In Texas state court we can either work with the district attorney’s office (if they are amenable) or argue against them to get a bail reduced.

What can I do while out on bail?

While out on bail you can do anything you want so long as the judge did not order otherwise. Typical bail requirements are that you not break any other laws, show up to your court dates and offense-specific requirements like no-alcohol for DWI offenses, no-contact orders for Assault crimes and no-travel restrictions for more serious crimes.

Can I travel while out on bail?

Typically you can travel while on bail, but it depends on whether the judge in your case ordered you not to travel while out on bail. If you need to travel for an emergency, then our criminal lawyer can typically work with the court if there is an existing travel ban.

When do you need to hire a criminal defense lawyer?

Waiting too long to hire a criminal defense lawyer is a common mistake that can severely impact the quality of your defense. Before you are formally arrested, the police will conduct an investigation. If we have an opportunity to conduct our investigation, we may be able to catch mistakes in the police investigation and potentially keep you from getting arrested in the first place.

There is also a period of time before the district attorney will file charges. You may or may not be arrested before charges are filed. If you hire us early, we may have an opportunity to prevent charges from being filed. In felony cases, there is a similar period of time before an indictment is filed.

The bottom line is that if you have an opportunity to hire a criminal defense attorney sooner rather than later, do not pass up the opportunity.

When do I have to go to court?

You have to go to court whenever the court orders you to be there. Your first court date will usually be set automatically by the court, but the next court dates will be set by a combination of your criminal defense lawyer, the state or federal prosecutors and the court itself.

Your first court date in Dallas county could be weeks or months after you were arrested. There are similar time periods in other counties, and it usually depends on the charge and how quickly the state’s investigation progresses. Court dates are usually separated by a few weeks.

Is my driver’s license suspended?

If you have been arrested for DWI, the state cannot suspend your license without a hearing unless you have missed the deadline to request an ALR hearing. You will be entitled to a hearing called an ALR Hearing, but you need to request it and request it quickly and correctly. Learn more about ALR hearings and license suspensions and more about our DWI Defense practice

FAQs ABOUT COURT SETTINGS

  • What do I wear?
  • What time do I need to get there?
  • What will happen?
  • Why do I need to be there?
  • What happens at an occupational driver’s license hearing?

What do I wear?

Our general advice is to wear your “Sunday Best” – whatever that means to you.

What time do I need to get there?

You need to be there on time. If you’re late, the court may issue a warrant for your arrest. Generally that means you should plan on arriving early to the building early enough to find parking, get through security and find your courtroom. Court buildings can be confusing, so if you have never been to court before, we suggest arriving to the building 30 minutes early.

Your attorney will likely arrive after you. This is completely normal. Unfortunately for everyone, all court settings are usually at the exact same time. And we have more than one client hearing every day. So we can’t get to everyone at the exact same time. We may also have court in multiple different counties on the same day, in which case we may be running quite late. Don’t worry about it. Please be patient. We promise we won’t forget about you. If you have concerns, please feel free to email or text us.

What will happen?

For most court settings, the attorney will speak with the State prosecutor privately, and sometimes both the State prosecutor and your attorney will speak to the judge. Sometimes these conversations with the judge are “on the record” and sometimes they’re “off the record.” Either party (the state or the defense) can request this audience to be on the record. But most often we’re just discussing administrative issues, and there’s nothing really in dispute, so it’s just an informal conversation.

Most often, our clients do not speak to anyone and just wait for us to be finished. Some courts will require you to “Announce” that you are present when your name is called (like they did in school). And other courts will simply require you to wait in a line to tell the bailiff that you’re there.

Do not leave court without speaking to your attorney, however. Your attorney will dismiss you. If you leave early, we might not be done handling your case, and you could be liable to have your bond held insufficient and a warrant issued for your arrest.

For some kinds of court hearings, such as occupational driver’s license hearings, we may need to ask you some questions “on the record.” This is what’s called a “prove up.” Basically what that means is that the court needs certain facts about your case to be recorded before granting you your requested relief (such as your occupational license). It’s no big deal – we will just ask you the same questions that we’ve already asked you, and all you have to do is respond truthfully. Basically we just read you the petition that you have already reviewed and ask you if all the information is correct.

Why do I need to be there?

The court requires you to be at most court settings. The judges get to control whether or not your attendance is required. Don’t shoot the messenger. They’re not our rules. We just tell you about them so that you don’t get in trouble.

What happens at an occupational driver’s license hearing?

At an occupational driver’s license hearing, we will just be asking you to confirm that the information you gave to us is correct. We’ll have your petition for an occupational driver’s license and just ask you whether all of the information on it is correct.

Criminal investigations are conducted by the various police agencies of the state and federal government in addition to the state district attorneys and federal prosecutors.

How to know if you’re under investigation for a crime in Texas

If you are under investigation for a crime, we can help protect you and your rights. But how do you know if you’re under investigation?

Every criminal case begins with an investigation by the police or some other law enforcement agency. Sometimes the investigation period is brief. For instance, in a DWI investigation, the investigation usually consists of “tailing” the car, questioning the driver and collecting physical evidence.

ARE YOU BEING INVESTIGATED FOR A CRIME?

In other cases the investigation may be longer. In this kind of investigation you may or may not be aware the police are investigating, and you may not know you are the target of the investigation. Law enforcement may ask to question you or cooperate in the investigation in other ways. It is important that you have a criminal defense attorney any time you are communicating with the police.

If You Are Under Investigation for a Crime, Do NOT Talk to the Police Without an Attorney

Throughout this process, the investigators will conduct interviews with potential witnesses and collect physical evidence. If you are being contacted by law enforcement as part of an investigation, you should consider calling us immediately before you cooperate. You do not have to have done anything wrong to be convicted of a crime. You may be the subject of an investigation without even knowing it.

Even if you want to cooperate, it is best to gather as much information as possible in advance. Bear in mind that police officers and law enforcement are trained to make arrests and put people in jail. They are not trained to advocate for you or look out for your best interests. Make the call early on to hire a criminal lawyer who will represent you and protect your rights in a criminal investigation.

Police agencies including city police officers, sheriff’s officers, Department of Public Safety (DPS) officers, Texas Rangers and state troopers typically conduct the initial investigation on the state level. On the federal level, agents from the FBI, DEA, DHS, ATF and Secret Service typically conduct the initial investigations. After a case has been filed, the initial investigating agencies typically hand off the investigation to state or federal prosecutors.

How do I know if I am being investigated for a crime in Texas?

The only way to know for certain whether you’re being investigated for a crime in Texas is to get confirmation from the investigating agency. However, even if you are given an answer, there is no way that you can be sure that they are telling you the truth. The police are allowed to lie to you. But you can usually assume that when police are asking you questions, you are under investigation.

If you are seriously concerned about whether you are under investigation, book a consultation with us today.

How can you find out if there is a warrant for my arrest?

The best way to find out whether you have an active warrant is to call the office of the investigating agency or sheriff’s office. Bail bondsmen will usually look up whether there is an active warrant on you free of charge. For federal cases, it is more difficult because investigations are conducted more secretively.

How can I keep my name out of the media?

We regularly hear requests from clients to do everything we can to keep their names out of the media. Public relations management is part of our regular criminal defense practice for all major crimes and clients at their request. We are also ready to employ a more aggressive media stance if the circumstances require to defend our clients.

It is patently unfair for the police and prosecutors to publicize trials and investigations before trial because it colors the jury pool. However, this happens with regularity. If you are under investigation for a crime, you need a criminal defense attorney skilled in managing this media onslaught. Some of our best successes are the ones that you have never heard about because our clients’ names did not make it to the media.

What do I do if there is a warrant out for my arrest? Should I turn myself in?

If there is an active warrant for your arrest, do not ignore it. You should call us immediately to determine what is best for you to do under the circumstances. Sometimes we advise our clients to turn themselves in, and we go to court together with them. In these types of situations our criminal lawyers are frequently able to have a PR Bond set, and sometimes we can get the entire jail book-in process waived. We cannot do this for every case, but we will need to discuss the options with you. It is better to address an outstanding warrant than ignoring it. You do not want to have the police bust down your door at night or come to arrest you at work.

Can I get a walk-through? What is book and release?

A walk through means the same thing as “book and release.” This is the process in which bail is set and posted at the same time or before you are booked into jail. This is the fastest way to resolve an outstanding warrant and get you back out to your life and loved ones. We offer this service to our clients.

Do I have to talk to the police or answer questions?

In short, no you do not have to answer questions that the police ask you when they are investigating a crime. However, not answering questions can look bad and the fact that you are uncooperative can be used against you. You expose yourself to risk by not cooperating, and sometimes the police will get angry and may even attempt to harm you. This is why it is best to have a criminal defense attorney before you even consider answering questions. If the police are trying to interrogate you or are asking you to cooperate in an investigation, call me immediately.

Do you need to hire a criminal lawyer?

You should be represented by a criminal lawyer from the moment that you are under investigation for a crime. In many circumstances, it may be difficult to know whether you are being investigated until it’s too late, so call us immediately if you have any concern about a pending investigation. If you have already been arrested or charged with a crime, you should not hesitate to hire a criminal defense lawyer. After you are arrested or charged with a crime, a criminal defense attorney can help protect your rights during an investigation by the police or other law enforcement agency. After you are arrested, a criminal lawyer can represent you in court and advise you about the best strategies to defend you and protect your freedom and all of your rights.

How do I defend myself and protect my rights during a police investigation?

If you have a lawyer, you should be able to preserve your rights through the protection of counsel. I usually advise my clients to tell the police that they have a lawyer and will be happy to cooperate with them if their lawyer allows it. This makes the police aware that my clients are represented by counsel and that they are willing to cooperate. In addition, I typically conduct a parallel investigation so that we do not rely on the law enforcement agency’s work alone. We collect evidence and interview witnesses favorable to us.
